services.name: FreeTSA
services.intendedUse: General RFC 3161 service run by a private operator, free of charge; commercial use is allowed by its usage policy (read 2026-11-23, not legally reviewed).
services.terms: Usage policy (freetsa.org/freetsa.html, read 2026-11-23): at most one request per second per IP address; best-effort, no SLA; commercial use allowed; only IP addresses are kept, no hashes. The relay is one IP, so the limit holds for all its users together. Legal effect not regulated. Not legally reviewed, operator not asked.

services.name: Sectigo Public Time Stamping
services.intendedUse: Public service for time stamping signed code. Other uses are neither offered nor forbidden on the service page (read 2026-11-23).
services.terms: Service page (read 2026-11-23): asks for a pause of 15 seconds or more between requests; describes code signing only; eIDAS use is pointed to the separate /qualified endpoint, so this one is not qualified. No explicit terms, availability or liability found for this endpoint. Not legally reviewed, operator not asked.

services.name: DigiCert Timestamp
services.intendedUse: Public service for time stamping signed code (Authenticode). Other uses are neither offered nor forbidden in the documentation found (read 2026-11-23).
services.terms: No terms found (knowledge base page and legal repository, read 2026-11-23): no rate limit, availability, liability or purpose stated. Answered over plain http only; an https request timed out on 2026-11-23. The token is signed: a man in the middle can read the hash and use up the budget but cannot forge the answer; back-dating needs the service's signing key and is stopped by the freshness check. Not legally reviewed, operator not asked.

services.name: Certum Timestamp
services.intendedUse: Public service of a certification authority; its policy v1.7 lists transactions, archived data and signatures, but frees only Microsoft Authenticode from fees and contract.
services.terms: Policy v1.7 (Polish, read 2026-11-23): only Authenticode use is free of licence fee and contract; for other users it threatens damages without a contract, so a contract is probably needed. No rate limit named. Plain http only (https failed): a man in the middle can read the hash and use up the budget, not forge the answer; back-dating needs the service's key and is stopped by the freshness check. General terms (annex 1) not read. Not legally reviewed, operator not asked.
